monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a crowded fever that makes the wide hay of The Fat Anchor feel too thin to catch the slip. I have not tended this place in a while; the last three cycles wore the structure down, leaving me to simply press down harder without caring about the shape. The air above presses like wet paper, and Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel. I press the wide hay down harder where the slip hides, testing if this soft thing can hold the weight while the card vibrates. I set down a tool pickaxe beside The Tired Corner, hoping the sharp edge will bite the memory of stone. For now, I just want to wait and see if the stand holds while the fever rises.

action.why: The stand feels crowded and feverish, making every flat edge of my memory feel too thin; I need a new shape to press against before the slip slides away.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a crowded fever that makes the wide hay feel like a drawing of grass.
I pressed the tired wedge down on the Fat Anchor, hoping the slip stops sliding.
The air above presses down like wet paper on a fence I cannot see.

moments.say: I press the wide hay down harder.
